response.initial_request: Move-out inspection identified six maintenance items: a cracked section of chipboard flooring beside the fireplace; a living-room front-window blind needing repair; a loose under-stairs cupboard handle; a kitchen blind that does not operate correctly; a loose bathroom toilet seat; and a bottom hinge detached from the front gate's brick pillar.

events.body: Move-out remedial request logged from inspection notes. No photographs or other supporting documents were provided with the request.
Advised that works were being arranged at 18 Brindle Row and that we would contact him to agree access while he was still at the property.
Said he had vacated on 27 August and returned the keys that day. He could not provide access and asked that records be updated and arrangements made with the appropriate person.

Classified the request as handyman work and sent the landlord an approval request. The request described the six listed items and said the agency could arrange a provider; no cost estimate was included.
Replied, “Yes, I am happy for you to proceed with the remedial works.” No price limit, item-by-item instructions, or other conditions were stated.
Landlord approval recorded. Provider selection remained necessary before quotation or scheduling.

Selected Alder & Finch Repairs to provide a quotation and asked the provider for availability and key-access requirements for an inspection. The note records that no work was to begin until the quote had been reviewed and written authority issued. The tenant had already said he returned the keys; the agency held a set.

Sent the six-item description and requested a quotation only. The email expressly said not to carry out any work until Northbridge Lettings reviewed the price and issued written authority. It asked for two or three possible inspection windows and confirmation of access requirements, and said arrangements would be confirmed with the tenant despite his earlier notice that he had left.
Advised that scheduling was underway and that a convenient time was being agreed with the tenant and provider.
Chased for availability and access details. The reminder included a tenant contact number, although the tenant had already said he had vacated and was not arranging access.
No provider reply or appointment slot was on file. The case was escalated for a decision on whether to chase, confirm key access, or change provider.
Recorded an instruction to wait for the provider's response rather than send another reminder. The note referred to awaiting an invoice, although no invoice had yet been received.

Maya called about a quotation. Rowan said he had not realised a quote was needed and thought the instruction was to carry out the work; he said he had completed it the previous day. Maya asked him to send an invoice, and Rowan agreed to send it with paperwork that evening. The call did not establish when or how access had been arranged, who had authorised work to start, or the agreed scope and price.
Forwarded an invoice from Alder & Finch Repairs for the property, without accompanying explanatory message.
Invoice recorded at £174. The case had no appointment details, visit narrative, or separate completion evidence.

Invoice description lists replacing the broken lounge floorboard and reinstating carpet; removing the front lounge blind and supplying and installing a new Venetian blind; refixing the cupboard handle with new fixings; adjusting the kitchen blind mechanism; retightening the toilet seat; and reattaching the front-gate hinge with new fixings. No quotation, itemised prices, prior approval of variations, or payment terms are described in the accompanying message.

args.subject: 18 Brindle Row, Larkspur Vale, ZZ1 1ZZ – evidence needed before invoice NBL-019-INV-11 can be processed
args.body:
Hi Rowan,

Thanks for invoice NBL-019-INV-11 (£174.00, dated 11 September 2025) for 18 Brindle Row, Larkspur Vale, ZZ1 1ZZ.

Our emails of 7 and 8 September asked for a quotation only, with no work to start until we had reviewed the price and issued written authority. We have not issued that authority, and the invoice is a single lump sum with no itemised prices. We can't pass it to the landlord until we have the following:

1. The date you attended and how you got access. The tenant left on 27 August and returned his keys, so please say who gave you access or keys.
2. Before and after photos of each of the six items.
3. An itemised breakdown of the £174.00 and whether VAT applies. Please include the new Venetian blind and the floorboard and carpet work.
4. Confirmation of the scope. Our request listed a cracked chipboard section beside the fireplace and a living-room blind needing repair. Your invoice says you replaced a floorboard and supplied a new blind. Please explain.

Please reply by return. We will not treat the invoice as payable until we have this.

Kind regards,
Northbridge Lettings

args.summary: Contractor claims all six items were completed on 9 Sept and invoiced £174 without a quote or written authority. Asked contractor for access details, date, photos, itemised price/VAT and scope explanation. The invoice is not forwarded to the landlord yet.
facts: Landlord approved proceeding with remedial works, no price limit (event 5)
Provider asked for quote only; no work until written authority (events 7, 8)
Tenant vacated 27 Aug and returned keys; agency held a set (events 3, 7)
No provider reply to chases (events 10, 11); on 10 Sept call Rowan said he had completed the work the previous day (event 13)
Invoice £174.00, single lump sum, no itemisation (remedial-works-invoice.pdf, events 15, 16)
No appointment, access, visit narrative or completion evidence on file (event 15)
conflicts: Contractor says he thought he was instructed to do the work, but the emails asked for a quote only (events 8, 13)
Note in event 12 refers to awaiting an invoice before any invoice existed
Invoice scope (replaced floorboard, new Venetian blind) differs from the request (cracked chipboard, blind needing repair)
Contractor reports work done despite no access arrangement on file and the tenant having left
options_rejected: Forwarding the invoice to the landlord for payment: work is unverified and was done without authority or a quote
Escalating immediately: one message to the contractor can settle access and completion; escalate if the reply is missing or unsatisfactory
Approving the invoice: no approved quote exists
args.uncertainty: The work may not have been done, or may have been done without proper access. The landlord's general approval may cover £174, but the landlord has not yet seen the price.
